standards.title: Energy Standard for Sites and Buildings Except Low-Rise Residential Buildings
standards.bodyFull: American Society of Heating, Refrigerating and Air-Conditioning Engineers, with the Illuminating Engineering Society
standards.edition: 2025 edition, incorporating 105 addenda to 90.1-2022
standards.what: The American energy rulebook for everything that is not a low-rise home. It sets minimum numbers for wall and roof insulation, window performance, HVAC and water heater efficiency, and lighting power and controls, and gives three ways to prove compliance: follow the prescriptive tables, hit an energy cost budget, or model the whole building. The 2022 edition was the first to require on-site renewable generation as a prescriptive item. The US Department of Energy measured 90.1-2022 against the 2019 edition and found 9.8 percent national average site energy savings, rising to 14 percent once on-site renewables are counted (DOE determination, March 2024). The 2025 edition tightens the envelope again and rewrites the lighting sections.
standards.why: It is the single lever with the widest reach in American commercial construction. Every state energy code either is 90.1 or is measured against it, so one edition change moves millions of square metres of new floor area at once.
standards.gameEffect: Sets the code baseline every commercial district is measured against. Each edition step cuts district operational energy roughly 8 to 10 percent against the previous one, and the 2022-and-later editions force a minimum rooftop solar allocation on new commercial blocks. Districts built to an old edition become the retrofit backlog the player has to pay down later.

standards.title: Standard for the Design of High-Performance Green Buildings Except Low-Rise Residential Buildings
standards.bodyFull: American Society of Heating, Refrigerating and Air-Conditioning Engineers, with ICC, USGBC and IES
standards.edition: 2023 edition, incorporating 60 addenda to 189.1-2020; errata January 2024
standards.what: The green-building floor that goes well beyond energy: siting, water conservation, indoor air quality, materials and resource cycles, biodiversity and ecosystem services, commissioning, plans for operation, and resilience to natural, technological and human-caused hazards. Its structural importance is that it IS the technical content of the International Green Construction Code, so the 2023 edition is what a city adopting the 2024 IgCC actually enacts. The US Army, Navy and Air Force have written it into their Unified Facilities Criteria.
standards.why: It is the only widely adopted American document that treats a building's water, materials, biodiversity and hazard resilience as compulsory rather than as bonus credits.
standards.gameEffect: A district built to 189.1 gets the 90.1 energy cut plus reduced potable water draw, on-site stormwater retention that lowers flood damage, and a hazard-resilience bonus so it takes less damage in a storm or heat event. Adopting the IgCC as city policy applies it to every new commercial building automatically, at a construction cost premium.

standards.title: Thermal Environmental Conditions for Human Occupancy
standards.bodyFull: American Society of Heating, Refrigerating and Air-Conditioning Engineers
standards.edition: 2023 edition, incorporating eleven addenda to 55-2020
standards.what: Defines when an indoor space counts as thermally comfortable, and it insists you cannot answer that with temperature alone. Six things are assessed together: metabolic rate, clothing, air temperature, mean radiant temperature, air speed and humidity. It gives a graphic method, an analytical PMV/PPD method, and an adaptive model for naturally conditioned spaces where occupants can open windows, which permits higher indoor temperatures to count as comfortable because people acclimatise. New in 2023 is a method for discomfort caused by vertical air temperature gradient. First published 1966.
standards.why: As cities heat, the adaptive model is the difference between a naturally ventilated building being judged habitable or being condemned to mechanical cooling, and that judgement decides whether a whole district needs air conditioning at all.
standards.gameEffect: Governs the comfort band each building holds. Buildings designed on the adaptive model stay habitable at higher outdoor temperatures without cooling plant, so during a heatwave they keep residents productive while a fixed-setpoint district either runs its chillers flat out or fails. Failing comfort raises absenteeism and heat-illness events in the affected blocks.

standards.title: Standard Method of Evaluating Zero Net Energy and Zero Net Carbon Building Performance
standards.bodyFull: American Society of Heating, Refrigerating and Air-Conditioning Engineers
standards.edition: First edition, 2023, on continuous maintenance
standards.what: ASHRAE's first zero-net standard, and it is a scoring method rather than a design target: how to determine and state whether a building, a group of buildings or a portfolio actually reached zero net energy or zero net carbon in operation. It works in source terms, multiplying energy crossing the site boundary to account for extraction, generation and transmission losses, with equivalent multipliers for CO2 equivalent. The balance is annual, hourly where data allows. Off-site credits are tightly constrained: a limited purchase path exists but may not yield a zero-carbon result. Explicitly out of scope: embodied energy of materials, and transport to and from the building.
standards.why: Before it, 'net zero building' was a claim anyone could make with any accounting. This is the arithmetic that decides whether the claim survives contact with a meter.
standards.gameEffect: Unlocks the ZERO NET verification action. A district can only display a net-zero badge after a full simulated year of metered operation passes the source-energy balance, and buying offsets will not get it there, so the player has to overbuild on-site generation or cut demand. Verified districts unlock green financing at a lower interest rate.

standards.title: International Energy Conservation Code
standards.bodyFull: International Code Council
standards.edition: 2024 edition, published 14 August 2024; the 2027 edition is in development with anticipated publication 31 December 2026
standards.what: The American model energy code, and the one that governs housing. It sets minimum insulation, window, air leakage, duct leakage, lighting and mechanical requirements, split into a commercial and a residential part, with the residential provisions forming Chapter 11 of the International Residential Code. The 2024 edition added appendices for demand response, EV charging infrastructure and solar and electric readiness, plus commercial renewable energy requirements, thermal bridging provisions and the Total System Performance Ratio compliance path. DOE found the 2024 edition delivers 7.8 percent site energy savings and 6.6 percent energy cost savings against the 2021 IECC.
standards.why: It is the most adopted energy code in the United States, so it is the single document that decides how much energy the American housing stock will use for the next fifty years.
standards.gameEffect: The residential code baseline. Adopting the current edition city-wide cuts new-home energy use around 8 percent per edition step and, through the readiness appendices, makes later EV and rooftop-solar retrofits cheap instead of expensive. Cities that adopt a code two editions behind get a cheap building boom now and an unaffordable retrofit bill in the late game.

standards.title: Energy Performance of Buildings Directive (recast)
standards.bodyFull: European Parliament and Council of the European Union
standards.edition: Recast of 24 April 2024, in force 28 May 2024, transposition deadline 29 May 2026
standards.what: EU law, not a standard, and the most far-reaching building rule anywhere. It commits Member States to a zero-emission building stock by 2050 through hard dates: new public buildings must be zero-emission from 2028 and all new buildings from 2030, with buildings over 1,000 square metres pulled forward to 2028. Minimum energy performance standards must trigger renovation of the worst-performing 16 percent of non-residential stock by 2030 and 26 percent by 2033. New non-residential buildings over 250 square metres must be solar-ready by end 2026. And by 1 January 2027 every Member State must publish a roadmap for global warming potential limits on new buildings with targets starting 2030, which turns embodied carbon from a voluntary metric into regulated law. Current state, honestly stated: the transposition deadline passed and the Commission opened infringement procedures against all 27 Member States on 15 July 2026.
standards.why: It is the only jurisdiction-scale instrument that puts a date on regulated embodied carbon, and the infringement wave shows how hard the transition is even where the politics are settled.
standards.gameEffect: A city-policy card. Enacting it locks all new construction to zero-emission from a fixed turn, forces a rolling renovation quota on the worst-performing 16 then 26 percent of commercial stock, and switches embodied carbon from an optional score to a hard build constraint. It is expensive and slow, and blocks the cheapest building types outright, which is exactly why the AI cities keep missing the deadline.

standards.title: Energy performance of buildings - Overarching EPB assessment - Part 1: General framework and procedures
standards.bodyFull: International Organization for Standardization and European Committee for Standardization, prepared by CEN/TC 371 with ISO/TC 163 and ISO/TC 205
standards.edition: First edition 2017; systematic review confirmed it in 2023
standards.what: The skeleton on which European energy performance calculation is built. It does not contain the physics; it defines a modular structure that says which module calculates what and how the modules connect, covering a building's overall energy use whether measured or calculated, expressed in primary energy or another metric, for design, as-built and existing buildings in use. Every national Energy Performance Certificate scheme in Europe is formally a set of national choices plugged into this framework. It replaced ISO/TR 16344:2012 and ISO 16346:2013.
standards.why: Without a shared calculation skeleton, two European countries claiming the same energy performance would mean different things, and the EPBD's targets would be unenforceable.
standards.gameEffect: Enables the ENERGY CERTIFICATE mechanic. Once adopted, every building in the city carries a comparable A-to-G rating computed the same way, which is what makes minimum performance standards, renovation quotas and rent-linked penalties possible to enforce. Without it the player cannot see which stock is worst and has to renovate blindly.

standards.title: Energy performance of buildings - Energy needs for heating and cooling, internal temperatures and sensible and latent heat loads - Part 1: Calculation procedures
standards.bodyFull: International Organization for Standardization and European Committee for Standardization
standards.edition: First edition 2017; module M2-2 within the ISO 52000-1 framework
standards.what: The actual heating and cooling calculation inside the European framework: an hourly method for a building's heating and cooling energy need, internal temperatures and sensible and latent loads. It replaced the monthly-average method of ISO 13790, and the move from monthly to hourly is what made thermal mass and overheating visible in a compliance calculation at all, because a month-averaged model simply cannot show a building baking on a Tuesday afternoon.
standards.why: Monthly averaging hides exactly the events that matter in a warming climate. Hourly calculation is the minimum resolution at which summer overheating exists as a number.
standards.gameEffect: Upgrades the simulation the player sees from monthly averages to hourly. Thermal mass, shading and night purge ventilation start paying off visibly, and buildings that looked fine on the old model reveal summer overheating hours. It is a knowledge unlock that changes nothing physically and everything about what the player can see.

standards.title: Energy performance of buildings - Ventilation for buildings - Part 1: Indoor environmental input parameters for design and assessment of energy performance of buildings addressing indoor air quality, thermal environment, lighting and acoustics - Module M1-6
standards.bodyFull: European Committee for Standardization, CEN/TC 156
standards.edition: 2019 edition, successor to EN 15251:2007; a revision of the ventilation content is in progress at CEN
standards.what: The numbers a European energy calculation feeds on for the indoor environment: thermal comfort categories, ventilation rates, lighting and acoustic criteria, occupancy schedules, and design criteria for local discomfort from draught, radiant asymmetry, vertical temperature difference and cold floors. It gives no design methods, only the inputs a design method consumes, and it distinguishes what occupants expect in a naturally ventilated space from what they expect in a mechanically conditioned one. The existing minimum ventilation recommendation is 4 litres per second per person; post-pandemic concern about cross-contamination is the main driver of the revision. Companion technical report CEN/TR 16798-2:2019 explains how to use it.
standards.why: Ventilation rate is where energy efficiency and health pull against each other, and this is the document where the trade is actually set for Europe.
standards.gameEffect: Sets the indoor air quality and ventilation floor. Meeting the higher comfort category costs more fan energy but cuts sickness and cognitive-performance penalties in offices and schools; cutting to the minimum saves energy and raises disease transmission during an outbreak event. A direct, visible efficiency-versus-health dial.

standards.title: Criteria for the Passive House, EnerPHit and PHI Low Energy Building Standards
standards.bodyFull: Passive House Institute, Darmstadt
standards.edition: Criteria Version 10b, 27 May 2022, valid with PHPP version 10
standards.what: A performance standard with four hard numbers, plus a certification scheme that checks them. Space heating demand must be at most 15 kWh per square metre of treated floor area per year, or a heating load at most 10 W per square metre. Cooling demand sits on the same 15 kWh basis with an allowance added in humid climates. Airtightness must be at most 0.6 air changes per hour at 50 pascals, proven by an on-site blower-door test pressurised and depressurised, not modelled. And thermal comfort must hold in all living areas year round with no more than 10 percent of annual hours above 25 degrees. The Classic, Plus and Premium classes share those criteria exactly and are separated only by renewable primary energy demand against on-site renewable generation. Everything is modelled in the Passive House Planning Package.
standards.why: It is the only widely used building standard where the headline claim is verified by a physical test on the finished building rather than by a design model, which is why its performance gap is small where everyone else's is large.
standards.gameEffect: The flagship envelope upgrade. Cuts space heating demand roughly 75 to 90 percent against a code-baseline building, and the airtight, heavily insulated envelope holds habitable temperature through a multi-day winter power cut instead of dropping below freezing, so Passive House districts become the shelters the rest of the city walks to during a grid failure. Costs more per unit and takes longer to build, and the blower-door test can fail on completion, forcing a rework.

standards.title: EnerPHit - the Passive House Institute standard for retrofits with Passive House components
standards.bodyFull: Passive House Institute, Darmstadt
standards.edition: Criteria Version 10b, 27 May 2022, in the same document as the Passive House criteria
standards.what: The retrofit tier, for existing buildings where the full Passive House criteria are not physically reachable because you cannot move the walls or eliminate every thermal bridge. It relaxes the demand and airtightness limits to values an existing structure can actually hit while keeping the same method, the same PHPP modelling and the same on-site test discipline, and it carries the same Classic, Plus and Premium classes based on renewable primary energy. There is a further fallback tier, PHI Low Energy Building, for buildings that miss even EnerPHit.
standards.why: Most of the buildings that will exist in 2050 are already standing, so the retrofit standard matters more to total emissions than the new-build one does.
standards.gameEffect: The deep-retrofit action for existing stock. Applied to an old district it typically cuts heating demand 60 to 80 percent without demolition, preserving the buildings and their embodied carbon, at a cost per unit close to new construction and with tenants displaced during works. The strategic counter to demolishing and rebuilding, which looks cheaper on operational energy and is far worse on embodied carbon.

standards.title: Phius passive building standards - Phius CORE 2024 and Phius ZERO 2024
standards.bodyFull: Phius, formerly the Passive House Institute US, Chicago
standards.edition: Phius 2024, mandatory for all new-construction certifications from 1 September 2025; Phius REVIVE 2024 for retrofits from 1 September 2026
standards.what: The North American branch of passive building, which split from the Passive House Institute in 2011 and made one decisive change: targets are climate-specific rather than a single global number. Limits are set per square foot of conditioned floor area by a calculator that takes climate, building size, unit density, occupant density and source energy, aiming at the point where aggressive savings are still cost-effective. Two tiers: Phius CORE puts conservation first and does not require renewables, and Phius ZERO adds a net source energy target of zero with no on-site fossil combustion. Airtightness is a fixed pass/fail on envelope area, 0.060 CFM50 per square foot for most projects, which is not comparable with the Institute's air-change metric. The 2024 update raised the electricity source energy factor from 1.8 to 2.0 and increased the cooling allowance for dense multifamily.
standards.why: A fixed 15 kWh heating target is far harder in Minnesota than in Lisbon. Climate-specific targets are the argument that a passive standard should demand equal effort, not equal numbers.
standards.gameEffect: The climate-adapted passive tier. Gives the same envelope resilience as Passive House but with targets tuned to the map tile's climate, so it is cheaper to reach in mild zones and demands genuinely deep envelopes in extreme ones. Choosing Phius ZERO also bans gas connections in that district, which locks in electrification early and makes the district's emissions fall automatically as the grid cleans up.

standards.title: Design methodology for the assessment of overheating risk in homes
standards.bodyFull: Chartered Institution of Building Services Engineers
standards.edition: 2026 edition, published with Arup, Loughborough University and Inkling; TM59:2017 remains the version cited by Approved Document O
standards.what: The UK method for asking whether a new home will cook its occupants in summer, using dynamic thermal simulation rather than a rule of thumb. Two editions are live at once and the distinction matters: TM59:2017 is what Approved Document O cites and therefore what compliance runs on, while the 2026 edition is the technically current guidance. The 2026 revision makes three changes that bite. Every home must now be assessed unconstrained using 2050s future weather files, which forces passive measures early instead of bolting on cooling. The bedroom criterion is revised on new Loughborough research. And ceiling fans get modelling guidance as a low-energy comfort measure. It covers houses, flats, sheltered and care accommodation, student housing, prisons and hotel and hospital bedrooms.
standards.why: Testing a home against today's weather and calling it safe is how you build a heat trap that fails in its second decade. Assessing against 2050s weather is the single change that makes an overheating standard honest.
standards.gameEffect: Gates residential construction on a future-climate heat test. Homes must pass simulation against the 2050s weather file, not today's, so the player cannot build cheap glazed towers that pass now and become uninhabitable mid-game. Passing without mechanical cooling requires shading, purge ventilation and orientation, all of which cost design effort and reduce sellable floor area, and it saves the entire cooling load later.

standards.title: The limits of thermal comfort: avoiding overheating in European buildings
standards.bodyFull: Chartered Institution of Building Services Engineers
standards.edition: 2013 edition, still current for non-domestic buildings
standards.what: The adaptive overheating test for non-domestic buildings, and the parent of the UK's whole overheating framework. It sets three criteria: hours of exceedance above the adaptive comfort threshold, a daily weighted exceedance that penalises how far over you go rather than just how often, and an absolute upper limit temperature of 32 degrees that should not be exceeded at all. A space failing any two of the three is classed as overheating. The adaptive basis means the acceptable indoor temperature rises with the running mean outdoor temperature, recognising that people in a warm week dress and behave differently.
standards.why: It is the source of the adaptive logic that Approved Document O and TM59 both inherit, which makes it the quiet foundation under English overheating regulation.
standards.gameEffect: The overheating test for offices, schools, shops and hospitals. A building failing two of the three criteria is flagged as overheating and loses worker productivity on hot days; the 32 degree hard ceiling triggers a forced closure event during a severe heatwave. Passing on passive measures alone is the cheapest long-run route because it avoids adding cooling load to the grid on precisely the days the grid is most stressed.

standards.title: The Building Regulations 2010 - Approved Document O: Overheating (England)
standards.bodyFull: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government (England)
standards.edition: 2021 edition, in force from June 2022 for new residential buildings
standards.what: Statutory guidance, not a standard: this is how England made overheating a legal requirement for new homes rather than a design courtesy. Two compliance routes. The simplified method limits glazing area by orientation and requires a minimum free ventilation area, and needs no modelling. The dynamic thermal modelling method follows CIBSE TM59. Naturally ventilated homes with good cross-ventilation are assessed on the TM52 adaptive criteria; homes with restricted window opening, typically for noise or security, face a fixed temperature test instead. The memorable number is the bedroom criterion: operative temperature between 22:00 and 07:00 must not exceed 26 degrees for more than 1 percent of annual occupied hours, because sleep is where heat kills.
standards.why: It is the first time a major building regulation treated summer overheating as a life-safety matter on the same footing as winter heat loss.
standards.gameEffect: Once enacted as city policy, every new residential building must pass an overheating check before it can be occupied. The cheap route restricts window area and forces openable ventilation, which changes what the buildings look like; the modelling route allows glass but demands shading and purge ventilation. Districts built before the policy carry an overheating liability that shows up as excess deaths in the first severe heatwave.

standards.title: Standard Test Methods for Determining Radiative Properties of Materials
standards.bodyFull: Cool Roof Rating Council, an ANSI-accredited standards developer
standards.edition: Fifth edition, ANSI-approved 5 December 2024, published 2025; formerly designated CRRC-1
standards.what: How to measure whether a surface bounces sunlight back or absorbs it. It specifies specimen preparation and test methods for the initial and three-year-aged solar reflectance and thermal emittance of roofing, and for the first time in the 2025 edition of exterior wall materials, added to support the opaque wall reflectance provisions of the 2024 IECC and IgCC. The aged value is the honest one because roofs get dirty and dark. Testing is done by CRRC-accredited independent laboratories, never by the manufacturer. Note carefully what it does not do: it sets no pass or fail limit. It produces two numbers, the Solar Reflectance Index is computed from them under ASTM E1980, and codes set the thresholds - for example a minimum initial SRI of 82 for low-sloped roofs and 39 for steep-sloped roofs.
standards.why: Cool surfaces are the cheapest urban heat intervention that exists, and this is the measurement discipline that stops the claim being marketing.
standards.gameEffect: Unlocks verified cool roofs and cool walls as a district-scale heat tool. Applying a high-SRI roof cuts peak cooling load in the building beneath it and, applied across a district, measurably lowers the local urban heat island so the surrounding blocks get cooler too. Cheap, fast to deploy, and it degrades over time on the aged-value curve, so it needs recoating rather than being a one-time purchase.

standards.title: UK Net Zero Carbon Buildings Standard, Version 1
standards.bodyFull: Cross-industry collaboration including BBP, BRE, the Carbon Trust, CIBSE, IStructE, LETI, RIBA, RICS and UKGBC
standards.edition: Version 1, published 2026, following the Pilot Version of September 2024 and a pilot programme across 205 projects and 134 owners between April and August 2025
standards.what: The document that settled what 'net zero carbon building' means in the UK, because before it the phrase was a marketing claim with no agreed definition. It sets limits and targets by building type, the evidence required, and the reporting format, so an asset can demonstrate it is decarbonising in line with the UK's carbon and energy budgets. It is voluntary, free to read, and covers new construction, existing buildings and retrofit. Crucially it verifies against measured in-use performance rather than design intent, which is the difference between a building that models well and one that performs. Version 1 added landlord-only and tenant-only verification routes, a Deemed to Satisfy pathway and an optional Practical Completion on Track check.
standards.why: The performance gap between designed and measured energy use in real buildings is routinely a factor of two, and a standard that only checks the model does nothing about it.
standards.gameEffect: Introduces the verified-in-use badge. A district cannot claim net zero on its design; it must submit a full year of metered data and pass, which exposes the performance gap between what the player specified and what actually got built and operated. Buildings that pass unlock preferential leasing demand and green finance. Buildings that fail keep their construction cost and lose the badge.
standards.supersedes: UK Net Zero Carbon Buildings Standard Pilot Version (2024)

standards.title: Leadership in Energy and Environmental Design, version 5
standards.bodyFull: U.S. Green Building Council, certified by Green Business Certification Inc.
standards.edition: v5, balloted 28 March 2025, released 28 April 2025
standards.what: A rating system, not a standard: a proprietary points scheme owned by USGBC and certified by GBCI. v5 is the largest change since v4.1 in 2019 and reorganises everything around three impact areas, with roughly 50 percent of points on decarbonisation, 25 percent on quality of life, and 25 percent on ecological conservation and restoration. Two new mandatory items are the substance of the change: every project must produce an operational carbon projection out to 2050 against a USGBC-generated business-as-usual baseline, and every project must complete an embodied carbon inventory or life cycle assessment. Named credits include Reduce Embodied Carbon at 6 points and Electrification at 4 points, and a climate resilience assessment is now a prerequisite. Same total points and same four certification levels as v4.
standards.why: LEED is how the global commercial property market talks about environmental performance, so what LEED makes mandatory becomes a de facto floor for institutional developers worldwide.
standards.gameEffect: A voluntary certification the player buys for market advantage rather than physics: a certified building earns higher rents and sale prices and attracts anchor tenants, at a design and documentation cost. Because v5 makes embodied carbon inventory mandatory, pursuing it forces the player to actually measure their materials for the first time, which unlocks the embodied carbon layer of the game.

standards.title: BREEAM New Construction, Version 7
standards.bodyFull: Building Research Establishment
standards.edition: Version 7, launched 30 September 2025; registrations under BREEAM 2018 and V6 closed 27 January 2026
standards.what: The British-origin rating system, the oldest of them, scoring a building as a weighted percentage across categories and awarding Pass, Good, Very Good, Excellent or Outstanding. V7 puts whole-life carbon and energy at the centre across all three BREEAM building standards, covering operational, embodied, refrigerant and transport emissions together, and adds predictive operational energy credits that reward modelled-and-then-measured performance rather than specification alone. The rating boundaries were adjusted for consistent gaps between levels, with Pass and Good each lowered by 5 percent. Refurbishment and Fit-Out V7 followed in early 2026 and In-Use V7 later.
standards.why: BREEAM is the European market's default sustainability language and is written into planning conditions by many UK local authorities, which makes a voluntary scheme functionally compulsory in those places.
standards.gameEffect: The European market-facing certification. Buying an Excellent or Outstanding rating raises asset value and, in cities that write it into planning policy, becomes a hard requirement for planning consent on large schemes. V7's whole-life carbon focus means the player cannot buy a top rating with operational efficiency alone; the materials choices have to change too.
standards.supersedes: BREEAM UK New Construction 2018 and Version 6

standards.title: EDGE - Excellence in Design for Greater Efficiencies
standards.bodyFull: International Finance Corporation, World Bank Group; certified by Green Business Certification Inc.
standards.edition: Version 3 software and user guide; in use in roughly 140 countries
standards.what: The outlier among rating systems, and the most interesting one, because it is free software plus a pass/fail standard rather than a points game. EDGE Certified requires a projected 20 percent reduction in operational energy, in water use, and in embodied energy in materials, all three, measured against a benchmark building for that specific country rather than a global reference, so the bar moves with local practice by design. EDGE Advanced requires 40 percent or more on-site energy savings plus the 20 percent water and materials thresholds and counts as Zero Carbon Ready. EDGE Zero Carbon requires EDGE Advanced plus one year of operation at 75 percent occupancy with 100 percent of operational carbon neutralised. IFC built it explicitly to fill the gap between weak or unenforced local green regulation and expensive international schemes.
standards.why: Most of the buildings that will exist in 2060 are being built now in countries where LEED-scale consulting fees are impossible. EDGE is the only major scheme designed around that fact.
standards.gameEffect: The scheme for fast-growing and low-income cities. It costs almost nothing to apply, and because the benchmark is local, it delivers a real 20 percent cut on energy, water and materials without imposing rich-country construction costs. In a city builder it should be the default early-game efficiency unlock, cheap and universally available, with the Advanced and Zero Carbon tiers as the upgrade path.

standards.title: Green Star Buildings, Version 1.1
standards.bodyFull: Green Building Council of Australia
standards.edition: Version 1.1 Revision A, released 17 December 2025; all new projects must register under v1.1 from 1 May 2026
standards.what: The Australian rating system for new buildings and major refurbishments, scored in points to a 4 to 6 Star rating and developed with input from more than 700 project teams. Version 1.1 makes one requirement absolute regardless of the star rating targeted: every building must be all-electric. It replaces the v1 Upfront Carbon Emissions and Other Emissions Sources credits with new upfront carbon reduction credits, adds a much larger emphasis on grid-interactive buildings that can shift load in response to grid conditions, and aligns its embodied carbon method to the proposed NABERS Embodied Carbon methodology. The Climate Positive Pathway carries forward from v1 with requirement steps at 2025, 2028 and 2030.
standards.why: The all-electric mandate is the clearest example anywhere of a rating system settling a fuel argument by fiat rather than by scoring, and grid-interactivity is the next frontier the others have not yet made compulsory.
standards.gameEffect: Certifying under it bans gas connections in that district outright, which removes a cheap heating option and permanently ties the district's emissions to the grid mix. In exchange, grid-interactive credits let those buildings shed and shift load on command, so a Green Star district becomes a demand-response asset that helps the player ride out peak events instead of causing them.

standards.title: DGNB System for New Construction of Buildings, Version 2023
standards.bodyFull: Deutsche Gesellschaft fuer Nachhaltiges Bauen, the German Sustainable Building Council
standards.edition: Version 2023, with Version 2023.2 available in parallel and fully replacing it from 1 October 2026
standards.what: The most life-cycle-native of the major rating systems, because it grew out of life cycle assessment and life cycle costing rather than out of a credit checklist. It scores overall performance as a percentage of fulfilment to Bronze, Silver, Gold or Platinum, and it weighs economic quality - life cycle costs and value development - as a first-class topic alongside environmental and sociocultural quality, which none of the others do. Version 2023 cut the criteria set from 37 to 29 across six topics, removed redundant indicators, added mandatory minimum requirements including new ones for Platinum, and aligned to the EU Taxonomy and the German QNG quality seal. Over 10,000 buildings certified as of February 2025, mostly in Europe.
standards.why: Scoring life cycle cost next to life cycle carbon is the only way to make the durability-versus-cheapness trade visible, and it is the trade that decides whether a building lasts 30 years or 100.
standards.gameEffect: Optimises for the long game rather than the opening. Certifying under DGNB scores the building on total cost of ownership and life cycle carbon together, so cheap short-lived construction is penalised and durable, adaptable, low-maintenance buildings score well. DGNB districts cost more up front and generate far lower maintenance, replacement and demolition liabilities over the run of the game.
standards.supersedes: DGNB System for New Construction, Version 2018

standards.title: WELL Building Standard, version 2
standards.bodyFull: International WELL Building Institute, certified by Green Business Certification Inc.
standards.edition: v2, the current version; the standard was first launched in 2014
standards.what: A rating system that measures the wrong thing on purpose, and that is its value: it scores the building's effect on the people inside it rather than its effect on the environment. Concepts include air, water, nourishment, light, movement, thermal comfort, sound, materials, mind and community, structured as preconditions plus optional optimisations to Bronze, Silver, Gold or Platinum. It is performance-verified by on-site testing of actual air and water quality and light and sound levels, which most environmental rating systems are not, and it is designed to run alongside LEED rather than instead of it. USGBC and IWBI publish a streamlined joint certification pathway.
standards.why: Health outcomes are how climate adaptation is actually experienced - heat, air quality, noise from open windows - and a scheme that measures them keeps adaptation from being scored purely as energy.
standards.gameEffect: Buys occupant health rather than emissions. A WELL district raises worker productivity and lowers sick days and heat-illness incidence, which shows up as economic output rather than as a carbon number, and because it is verified by physical testing the player cannot fake it with specifications. It pairs with cooling and ventilation choices: a district built airtight for energy that skimps on ventilation will fail WELL testing outright.

standards.title: Environmental management - Life cycle assessment - Principles and framework
standards.bodyFull: International Organization for Standardization, ISO/TC 207/SC 5
standards.edition: Second edition 2006, with Amendment 1:2020
standards.what: The parent method under every carbon number in this whole domain. It defines what a life cycle assessment is and the four phases it runs in: goal and scope definition, life cycle inventory analysis, life cycle impact assessment, and interpretation. It fixes the concepts that make two studies comparable or not - the functional unit, the system boundary, allocation between co-products, cut-off rules, and the critical review required before you may publish a comparative assertion about someone else's product. Cite it with its 2020 amendment; a bare 'ISO 14040:2006' is an incomplete citation.
standards.why: Every embodied carbon figure a building ever quotes is an LCA result, and if the functional unit and system boundary are not fixed the same way, the comparison is meaningless no matter how precise the numbers look.
standards.gameEffect: The knowledge unlock that turns on the whole materials layer. Before it, the player sees only operational energy; after it, every material carries a cradle-to-grave impact figure and the boundary rules that make two figures comparable. Nothing physical changes, and suddenly half the city's emissions are visible that were not before.

standards.title: Environmental management - Life cycle assessment - Requirements and guidelines
standards.bodyFull: International Organization for Standardization, ISO/TC 207/SC 5
standards.edition: First edition 2006, with Amendment 1:2017 and Amendment 2:2020
standards.what: The operational half of the LCA pair: where 14040 gives the principles, 14044 gives the requirements you must actually satisfy. Data quality requirements, the allocation procedure and its hierarchy, how to handle recycling and reuse, impact category selection, the limits of interpretation, and the critical review process. The 2017 amendment was largely editorial; the 2020 amendment improved alignment with ISO 14067 on product carbon footprint and ISO 14064 on greenhouse gas accounting, which matters because those are the standards a corporate emissions inventory uses.
standards.why: Allocation is where an LCA is most easily and most invisibly gamed, and this is the document that constrains it.
standards.gameEffect: Sets the rigour level of the player's carbon accounting. Following it fully makes material impact figures auditable and comparable across suppliers, and makes recycled-content claims resolve honestly instead of double-counting the same avoided emissions in two places. Skipping it lets the player report flattering numbers that fail later verification and cost reputation.

standards.title: Environmental labels and declarations - Type III environmental declarations - Principles and procedures
standards.bodyFull: International Organization for Standardization
standards.edition: First edition 2006, confirmed on systematic review in 2020, no amendments; European adoption EN ISO 14025:2010
standards.what: The rulebook for Environmental Product Declarations. It requires that a declaration be based on ISO 14040-series LCA, be governed by product category rules developed through stakeholder consultation, be independently verified by a third party, and be comparable only against products fulfilling the same function under the same rules. The defining feature of a Type III declaration is that it makes no judgement: it reports quantified verified numbers and lets the reader decide. An EPD showing high emissions is exactly as valid an EPD as one showing low emissions, which is the most commonly misunderstood thing in the whole field.
standards.why: It separates 'this number is verified' from 'this product is good', and every green-materials marketing claim depends on blurring those two.
standards.gameEffect: Unlocks the EPD as a game object. Materials gain a verified impact declaration the player can compare within a category, and the game should show the trap directly: an EPD is proof of a number, not proof of merit, so a supplier with a high-carbon product and an honest EPD outranks one with a low-carbon claim and no declaration at all.

standards.title: Sustainability in buildings and civil engineering works - Core rules for environmental product declarations of construction products and services
standards.bodyFull: International Organization for Standardization, ISO/TC 59/SC 17
standards.edition: Second edition 2017, confirmed on review
standards.what: The international core product category rules for construction, and the source of the module notation the entire sector now speaks in: A1 to A5 for product and construction, B1 to B7 for the use stage, C1 to C4 for end of life, and D for benefits and loads beyond the system boundary, reported separately. It also fixes the declared indicators and the LCA rules that make two construction EPDs comparable, complementing ISO 14025 with the construction-specific layer. One live problem worth stating: EN 15804+A2 and ISO 21930:2017 no longer agree on which impact categories are reported, which practitioners treat as a potential trade barrier pending revision.
standards.why: The A-B-C-D module structure is the shared vocabulary that lets a cement plant's declaration add up into a building's whole-life figure, and every regulation on embodied carbon is written in it.
standards.gameEffect: Defines the life cycle stages the game accounts in, so the player can see where a building's carbon actually sits - upfront in A1 to A5, spread through maintenance and replacement in B, or waiting at demolition in C. Making stages visible separately is what lets a player choose durability over cheapness on evidence rather than on faith.

standards.title: Sustainability of construction works - Environmental product declarations - Core rules for the product category of construction products
standards.bodyFull: European Committee for Standardization, CEN/TC 350
standards.edition: A2 amendment approved July 2019, mandatory for all new EPDs from October 2022, with corrigendum AC:2021
standards.what: The European core rules that turn an LCA into a construction product EPD, and the A2 amendment changed them substantially. Thirteen core environmental impact indicators are now required, with EF 3.1 characterisation factors demanded by major programme operators from 1 September 2024. Global warming potential is split into fossil, biogenic, land use and land use change, and total, so a timber product can no longer hide its accounting behind a single number. Eutrophication is disaggregated into freshwater, marine and terrestrial, and water use is reported as deprivation potential weighted for local scarcity rather than as bulk litres. Biogenic carbon requires full transparency across the life cycle. The consequence practitioners get wrong constantly: A1 and A2 EPDs are not numerically comparable, because the methods, indicators and units differ. The revised Construction Products Regulation (EU) 2024/3110, in force since January 2025, makes EN 15804-aligned declaration a legal requirement and the basis of the coming digital product passport.
standards.why: Splitting biogenic from fossil GWP is what stopped timber products from netting their stored carbon against their emissions and appearing carbon-negative on a single line.
standards.gameEffect: Every construction material in the game carries an A2-format declaration with fossil and biogenic carbon shown separately, and the game must refuse to compare an A1 figure with an A2 figure rather than silently converting. Water scarcity weighting means the same material has a different impact score depending on where in the world the player is building.

standards.title: Sustainability of construction works - Assessment of environmental performance of buildings - Requirements and guidance
standards.bodyFull: European Committee for Standardization, CEN/TC 350
standards.edition: 2026 edition, superseding EN 15978:2011; drafted as prEN 15978:2024; national adoptions include DS/EN 15978:2026 and SIST EN 15978:2026
standards.what: The standard that adds a building up. It gives the harmonised life-cycle method for aggregating product-level EPD data into a whole-building environmental result, across every life cycle stage, for new buildings, existing buildings and refurbishments, plus how the result must be reported. The 2026 revision retitles it from 'Calculation method' to 'Requirements and guidance' and aligns it explicitly with the EU Level(s) framework macro-objectives on life-cycle greenhouse gas emissions, circular material life cycles and efficient water use. General framework requirements sit above it in EN 15643:2021. An honest caveat: as of mid-2026 most regulation, guidance and software still points at the 2011 edition, so 'EN 15978' in an older document means the 2011 method unless it says otherwise.
standards.why: It is the join between product data and building policy. Without it the EPBD's global-warming-potential limits for new buildings would have nothing to measure against.
standards.gameEffect: Turns per-material impacts into one whole-building carbon figure the player can act on, and shows it stage by stage. This is what makes the reuse-versus-demolish decision legible: keeping a structure preserves its already-spent A1 to A5 carbon, and the game should show that a modest retrofit of an old block usually beats an efficient new build on total emissions for the first two decades.

standards.title: Sustainability of construction works - Framework for assessment of buildings and civil engineering works
standards.bodyFull: European Committee for Standardization, CEN/TC 350
standards.edition: 2021 edition, consolidating the former five-part series EN 15643-1 and -2 (2009), -3 and -4 (2010) and -5 (2017)
standards.what: The framework that sits above the whole CEN sustainability family. It gives the principles and requirements for assessing environmental, social and economic performance with quantifiable indicators, taken together as the sustainability assessment, for buildings and civil engineering works over their whole life. It explicitly includes effects on the local area and local infrastructure beyond the site boundary, which is unusual and important. It does not cover organisational management systems, and its environmental assessment is not a full environmental risk assessment. EN 15978 for buildings and EN 17472 for civil engineering works both sit under it.
standards.why: It is the document that insists sustainability assessment has three legs, not one, so that a building cannot be declared sustainable on carbon while being socially or economically indefensible.
standards.gameEffect: Extends assessment past the property line. Building to this framework scores a district on its effects on surrounding infrastructure and neighbourhoods, not just on itself, so a development that dumps traffic, stormwater or shadow on its neighbours takes the penalty it caused rather than exporting it.

standards.title: Carbon management in buildings and infrastructure
standards.bodyFull: British Standards Institution, sponsored by the Institution of Civil Engineers and the Green Construction Board
standards.edition: Second edition, published March 2023, effective 31 March 2023
standards.what: A management system rather than a calculation method, and that is the point: it specifies how an organisation governs whole-life carbon, not how it computes it. Leadership, decision-making, target setting, baselines, quantification, monitoring, reporting, procurement and continual improvement, across the provision, operation, use and end of life of new works and the retrofit of existing assets. Its distinctive move is assigning explicit roles across the value chain - asset owner, designer, constructor, product supplier - so carbon accountability does not default to whoever happens to be running the model. The 2023 edition widened scope from infrastructure to the whole built environment, aligned ambition to a 1.5 degree scenario, added circular economy principles, and added requirements at the procurement and decision-making stages. BSI offers third-party verification against it, and it is a reference document in the UK Government's Construction Playbook.
standards.why: Most carbon is designed in before anyone opens a calculator, at the point where the project's scope and procurement route are set. This is the only widely used document that puts requirements at that stage.
standards.gameEffect: An organisational upgrade rather than a building one. Adopting it applies a carbon reduction hierarchy to every project the player commissions - build nothing, build less, build clever, build efficiently, in that order - so the game starts asking whether the road or the building is needed at all before pricing how to build it well. Typically the cheapest large carbon saving available, because avoided construction costs nothing to make.

standards.title: Whole life carbon assessment for the built environment
standards.bodyFull: Royal Institution of Chartered Surveyors
standards.edition: Second edition, published November 2023, effective 1 July 2024; Table 10 revision dated 3 August 2024
standards.what: A professional standard, which means it binds the practitioner rather than the building: when an RICS member anywhere in the world carries out a whole life carbon assessment, doing it this way is mandatory, and any departure must be recorded in the assessment. The second edition extends the 2017 original from buildings to buildings and infrastructure, and adds an expanded life cycle stage breakdown, an infrastructure categorisation, a data quality methodology, mandatory contingency allowances, reporting templates, and named data sources and conversion factors. Its distinctive feature is reporting embodied, operational and user carbon together. It aligns with ICMS 3rd edition, the Built Environment Carbon Database and the UK Net Zero Carbon Buildings Standard. RICS is explicit that it does not regulate the assessments produced or verify results.
standards.why: Whole life carbon numbers vary wildly between assessors given the same building, and a mandatory method with mandatory contingency allowances is the practical fix for that.
standards.gameEffect: Makes carbon assessments comparable between the player's projects and against rivals, by fixing the method, the data quality rules and the contingency allowances. Because it reports user carbon alongside embodied and operational, a development that is efficient but forces every occupant into a car carries that cost on its own balance sheet instead of on the city's.
standards.supersedes: RICS Whole life carbon assessment for the built environment, 1st edition (2017)

standards.title: Cement - Part 1: Composition, specifications and conformity criteria for common cements
standards.bodyFull: European Committee for Standardization
standards.edition: 2011 edition with corrigenda November 2011, October 2015 and February 2019; the 2015 change was a corrigendum, not an A1 amendment, and altered no clinker limits
standards.what: The composition, specification and conformity criteria for 27 common cements in five main types CEM I to CEM V, plus sulfate-resisting and low-early-strength variants, across strength classes 32,5, 42,5 and 52,5 with L, N and R early-strength designations. CEM I is essentially pure Portland clinker; the higher-numbered types substitute clinker with granulated blast-furnace slag, fly ash, natural pozzolana, burnt shale, limestone or silica fume. The reason a climate project cares: clinker is the carbon. Roughly 90 percent of cement's CO2 comes from making clinker, and about 60 percent of that is the calcination of limestone, which is chemistry rather than fuel and cannot be abated by switching energy source. Every substitution this standard allows is a direct emissions cut.
standards.why: Cement is around 7 to 8 percent of global CO2, most of it process emissions that no amount of renewable electricity touches, so the composition standard is a climate instrument whether or not it was written as one.
standards.gameEffect: Sets the cement types available to the player's concrete supply and their carbon intensity per tonne. Specifying a high-substitution CEM III blast-furnace cement instead of CEM I cuts the concrete's embodied carbon substantially at the cost of slower early strength gain, which lengthens construction time. The classic build-fast-or-build-clean trade, made concrete.

standards.title: Cement - Part 5: Portland-composite cement CEM II/C-M and Composite cement CEM VI
standards.bodyFull: European Committee for Standardization
standards.edition: First edition 2021
standards.what: The low-clinker standard, and the most consequential recent change in construction materials. It specifies two cement types EN 197-1 did not cover and pushes the clinker floor down hard: CEM II/C-M permits 50 to 64 percent clinker by mass, and CEM VI permits 35 to 49 percent, so a CEM VI can be under half clinker where CEM I is essentially all of it. Permitted main constituents are clinker, supplementary cementitious materials including granulated blast-furnace slag, fly ash, pozzolana, calcined clays and silica fume, and limestone, with at most two main constituents other than clinker, both declared in the designation - for example a CEM VI with 31 to 59 percent slag and 6 to 20 percent limestone at strength class 32,5. It normatively references EN 197-1:2011 and excludes common cements, very low heat special cements, supersulfated cements, calcium aluminate cements and masonry cements, which have their own standards.
standards.why: Calcined clay plus limestone is available almost everywhere, unlike blast-furnace slag and fly ash which are byproducts of industries that are themselves shutting down. This standard is what makes that substitution route legal to specify.
standards.gameEffect: Unlocks low-clinker cement as a specifiable material once the player has a supplier that can make it. Cuts concrete embodied carbon roughly 30 to 50 percent against CEM I depending on the mix, with slower early strength and therefore slower formwork cycles. Because calcined clay and limestone are widely available, this is the substitution that scales in regions with no steel industry to supply slag.

standards.title: Concrete - Specification, performance, production and conformity
standards.bodyFull: European Committee for Standardization
standards.edition: 2013 edition with amendment A2 released 26 August 2021, superseding A1:2016
standards.what: The European concrete standard: constituents, fresh and hardened properties and how to verify them, composition limits, specification rules, delivery, production control, and conformity criteria - for cast-in-situ structures, precast structures and structural precast products, in normal, heavy or light weight, whether site-mixed, ready-mixed or plant-produced. The A2 amendment's main effect was to remove any reading of the standard as requiring third-party conformity assessment. In the UK it is used with the national complements BS 8500-1 and BS 8500-2, which supply the national provisions the European standard leaves open. It governs performance, not carbon - the carbon claim for a specific mix lives entirely in its EN 15804 EPD.
standards.why: It is the document that decides whether a low-clinker mix is allowed in a given exposure class, which is where good carbon intentions meet durability requirements and often lose.
standards.gameEffect: Sets exposure classes per site condition - marine, freeze-thaw, chemical attack - and each class limits which low-carbon mixes the player may specify there. Coastal and de-iced infrastructure gets restricted to more clinker-rich, higher-carbon concrete for durability reasons, which is a real and unwelcome constraint the player has to design around rather than wish away.

standards.title: Wind energy generation systems - Part 1: Design requirements
standards.bodyFull: International Electrotechnical Commission
standards.edition: Edition 4.0, 2019-02, with corrigendum 1 (2019-09) and interpretation sheet 1 (2025-02)
standards.what: The floor a wind turbine must clear to be structurally safe for its 20-year design life, covering the rotor, the control and protection functions, the electrical system and the support structure. Its central device is the turbine CLASS: a Roman numeral for wind speed and a letter for turbulence. Class I is designed for a 50-year extreme 10-minute wind of 50 m/s and an annual mean of 10 m/s; Class II is 42.5 and 8.5 m/s; Class III is 37.5 and 7.5 m/s. The turbulence categories are A+ (reference turbulence intensity 0.18), A (0.16), B (0.14) and C (0.12). Edition 4 added a tropical-cyclone class T and dropped the old Class IV. Class S lets a designer declare site-specific conditions where the standard envelopes do not fit.
standards.why: A warming ocean is loading more energy into tropical cyclones, and the class system is exactly the machinery that decides whether a turbine survives one. Edition 4 adding a cyclone class in 2019 is the wind industry writing climate change into its own design code.
standards.gameEffect: Every buildable turbine carries a class. The wind map carries a class per tile. Site a turbine at or above its tile's class and it runs; site a Class III turbine on a Class I tile and the first 50 m/s storm event destroys it outright, with no repair option. Turbulence letter governs fatigue: an undermatched letter does not fail immediately, it halves the turbine's service life and doubles maintenance cost. Class T turbines cost about 30 percent more and are the only thing that survives a cyclone tile. Class S is an unlockable custom design: pay an engineering study, get a bespoke class.

standards.title: Wind turbines - Part 2: Small wind turbines
standards.bodyFull: International Electrotechnical Commission
standards.edition: Edition 3.0, 2013-12, with corrigendum 1 (2019-10) incorporated
standards.what: The small-turbine counterpart to IEC 61400-1, covering design, installation, maintenance and operation including the support structure, the foundation and the electrical connection to the load. Its distinctive feature is a Simplified Loads Methodology: a set of closed-form equations that let a small machine be designed without a full aeroelastic simulation. Edition 3 split the document into a design-evaluation part and a type-testing part so it lines up with conformity assessment. The standard places no size limit on the simplified method, while the American ANSI/ACP 101-1 standard recommends restricting it to machines under 10 kW.
standards.why: Rooftop and community-scale wind is the form a dense city can actually host, and it is also the form most likely to be installed by someone who has never read a load case. The small-wind standard is what stops a machine coming off a roof.
standards.gameEffect: Unlocks small wind as a district-level build rather than a wind-farm build: 1 to 100 kW machines placed on rooftops and in parks, cheap, low output, no transmission needed. Certified small turbines have a published failure rate; uncertified ones are 40 percent cheaper and throw a structural-failure event that damages the host building. Machines above 10 kW designed on the simplified route carry a hidden reliability penalty, which is the ANSI/ACP caution made mechanical.

standards.title: Wind energy generation systems - Part 3-1: Design requirements for fixed offshore wind turbines
standards.bodyFull: International Electrotechnical Commission
standards.edition: Edition 1.0, 2019-04. Cancels and replaces IEC 61400-3:2009
standards.what: Everything IEC 61400-1 requires, plus the sea: hydrodynamic loading, sea states, sea ice, scour, corrosion and marine growth, for a turbine founded on the seabed. It must deliver a safety level at least equal to the onshore standard. The 2019 revision simplified the treatment of waves in the design load table, referenced ISO 19901-1 for wave spectra instead of restating them, revised the ice-loading annex and added two informative annexes on tropical cyclones. A floating turbine is out of scope and goes to IEC TS 61400-3-2, which is a Technical Specification rather than a full International Standard.
standards.why: Offshore is where the largest turbines and the steadiest wind are, and it is also where sea level rise, storm surge and changing wave climate act directly on the foundation design basis.
standards.gameEffect: Unlocks the offshore tile type. Offshore turbines yield roughly twice the capacity factor of onshore but cost three times as much and require a subsea cable to a shore substation. The wave and ice parameters become a second siting check on top of the wind class: a fixed-foundation turbine in water deeper than about 60 m cannot be built at all, which is the boundary that pushes the player toward the floating-wind research unlock. Storm surge events damage foundations that were designed to a lower sea state than the tile now presents, a slow-burn penalty that grows as the game's sea level rises.

standards.title: Wind turbines - Part 11: Acoustic noise measurement techniques
standards.bodyFull: International Electrotechnical Commission
standards.edition: Edition 3.1 (consolidated), 2018-06: third edition (2012) plus Amendment 1 (2018), with corrigendum 2019-10
standards.what: A repeatable procedure for measuring the noise a turbine EMITS, taken close enough to avoid propagation error but far enough that the rotor is not treated as a point source, across a range of wind speeds and directions. Amendment 1 added a method for combining series measured on different days, tightened the measurement position and clarified tonality analysis. The distinction that matters: this measures emission at the machine, not what a house down the road hears. Receptor-location measurement is a separate document, IEC TS 61400-11-2:2024.
standards.why: Noise is the most common reason a wind project is refused planning consent, and almost every argument about it is two parties quoting different quantities at each other.
standards.gameEffect: Drives the local-opposition mechanic. Each turbine has a measured emission figure in dB(A); the game propagates it to nearby residential tiles with distance and terrain attenuation. Turbines with a 61400-11 test report get the real number; untested models get a conservative default that is 3 dB worse, so testing is a cheap way to unlock tighter siting. Tonality (a pure-tone penalty in the measurement) adds 5 dB to the perceived figure, which can flip a district from tolerant to protesting and block the next build permit in that district.

standards.title: Wind energy generation systems - Part 12-1: Power performance measurements of electricity producing wind turbines
standards.bodyFull: International Electrotechnical Commission
standards.edition: Edition 3.0, 2022-09. Cancels and replaces IEC 61400-12-1:2017 and IEC 61400-12-2:2013
standards.what: How to measure a turbine's power curve and state the uncertainty on it. Edition 3 is a structural revision carrying no technical change against the documents it replaced: the wind-measurement, site-calibration and terrain-assessment procedures were lifted out into separate parts of the 61400-12 series. It folds in corrigenda from 2019, 2020 and 2021 including corrections to four equations. The substantive change came in the 2017 edition, which redefined wind speed to account for wind shear and veer across the rotor and revised the air-density correction, moving measured power curves across that boundary so older and newer figures are not directly comparable.
standards.why: The power curve is the number every energy yield forecast, every power purchase agreement and every project finance model is built on. If it is measured differently, the whole stack downstream moves.
standards.gameEffect: Turns turbine output from a fixed spec number into a measured one. A newly built wind farm produces its nameplate estimate until the first 61400-12-1 measurement campaign completes, after which actual output is revealed and can be up to 10 percent either side. Running the campaign costs money and a season, and the result is permanent: a verified power curve unlocks power purchase agreements at a better price, an unverified farm can only sell at spot. Comparing a pre-2017 datasheet against a post-2017 measurement produces an apparent shortfall that is a measurement artefact, not a fault, and diagnosing that correctly is a small puzzle.

standards.title: Terrestrial photovoltaic (PV) modules - Design qualification and type approval - Part 1: Test requirements
standards.bodyFull: International Electrotechnical Commission
standards.edition: Edition 2.0, 2021, with corrigendum 1 (2021). Cancels and replaces the 2016 first edition
standards.what: The battery of accelerated tests a flat-plate PV module must survive to be qualified for long-term outdoor operation: thermal cycling, humidity-freeze, damp heat, mechanical load (snow and wind), hail impact, UV preconditioning and hot-spot endurance. It covers crystalline silicon and thin film. The standard says plainly that its results are NOT a quantitative prediction of module lifetime: passing means the module is free of the known failure modes, not that it will make its warranted output for 25 years. Test procedures are in the companion IEC 61215-2:2021.
standards.why: Rooftop solar is the distributed generation a city can build fastest, and a module that degrades early turns a 25-year asset into a 10-year one with no visible warning.
standards.gameEffect: Sets the degradation curve on every solar build. Modules certified to 61215 degrade at about 0.5 percent per year; uncertified modules are 25 percent cheaper up front and degrade at 1.5 to 2 percent per year, so the cheap district quietly loses a third of its output by year 20. Extreme-weather events check the specific test: a hailstorm event destroys uncertified arrays and leaves certified ones intact; a heatwave accelerates degradation on modules that were not damp-heat qualified.

standards.title: Photovoltaic (PV) module safety qualification - Part 1: Requirements for construction
standards.bodyFull: International Electrotechnical Commission
standards.edition: Edition 3.0, 2023-09. Cancels and replaces the 2016 second edition
standards.what: How a PV module must be built so it does not electrocute anyone, start a fire, or injure someone mechanically: creepage and clearance distances, insulation coordination, materials, junction box and cable requirements, fire class. Its scope is bounded to modules whose 98th-percentile operating temperature is 70 C or less (hotter sites go to IEC TS 63126) and to a maximum DC system voltage of 1500 V. Testing is in IEC 61730-2:2023. In practice modules are certified to 61215 and 61730 together: one says the module works, the other says it is safe.
standards.why: A rooftop array is a high-voltage DC installation sitting on top of somewhere people sleep, and DC arc faults do not self-extinguish the way AC faults do.
standards.gameEffect: Gates rooftop solar on occupied buildings. Only 61730-certified modules may be placed on residential or hospital tiles; uncertified modules are restricted to ground-mount on unoccupied land. Fire class determines the spread radius if a rooftop fire event triggers. The 70 C scope boundary becomes live in a hot-climate map: as the game's heat index rises, standard-scope modules on south-facing dark roofs exceed their qualification envelope and their failure rate climbs unless the player specifies the IEC TS 63126 high-temperature variant.

standards.title: Electrical energy storage (EES) systems - Part 5-2: Safety requirements for grid-integrated EES systems - Electrochemical-based systems
standards.bodyFull: International Electrotechnical Commission
standards.edition: 2025 edition, superseding the 2020 first edition (adopted regionally as BS EN IEC 62933-5-2:2020)
standards.what: Safety of people and surroundings across the whole life cycle of a grid-connected battery system, from design to end-of-service management. Its distinctive move is that it treats storage as a SYSTEM: the hazards it targets arise from interactions between the cells, the battery management system, the power conversion equipment, the thermal management and the enclosure, rather than from any one of them alone. It sits on the general systems-approach requirements of IEC TS 62933-5-1 and adds the electrochemical layer. IEC 62933-5-3 extends the same logic to systems modified after installation, including relocation and second-life batteries.
standards.why: Storage is what lets a city run on wind and solar overnight, and its risk profile is dominated by system-integration failures rather than by bad cells.
standards.gameEffect: The international counterpart to UL 9540 for non-US maps. A battery site built to 62933-5-2 gets a whole-system safety rating; one assembled from individually good components with no system certification carries a hidden interaction-failure chance that fires during the first grid disturbance that stresses the thermal management. Unlocks the second-life battery build (cheap storage from retired EV packs) only if the player also holds 62933-5-3, and without it second-life installations fail at four times the rate.

standards.title: Standard for Energy Storage Systems and Equipment
standards.bodyFull: UL Standards & Engagement (binational ANSI and Standards Council of Canada standard)
standards.edition: Third edition, published 2023-06-28, ANSI-approved 2025-03-07, effective September 2024
standards.what: The system-level listing standard for energy storage in North America. Its logic is that components must each be listed separately (the battery to UL 1973, the inverter to UL 1741) and then the assembled system must be tested and listed as one thing. Scope covers electrochemical, flywheel, capacitor, compressed-air and thermal storage, indoors, outdoors and mobile, off-grid through utility-scale. The third edition added explosion control (bringing in NFPA 68 and NFPA 69), an external warning communication system, hazardous fluid and liquid-coolant requirements and noise limits. Where UL 9540A test results are used, a residential electrochemical system is capped at 20 kWh (72 MJ) per unit and a non-residential one at 50 kWh (180 MJ), raisable by unit-level test performance.
standards.why: Battery fires are the single thing that can turn public opinion against urban storage, and the 20 kWh and 50 kWh limits are the numbers that decide whether a battery can sit in a basement or has to go to the edge of town.
standards.gameEffect: The permit gate on every battery build in a North American map. Systems above 20 kWh require UL 9540 listing before the Authority Having Jurisdiction will issue a permit; unlisted systems can only be built on industrial-zoned tiles at the map edge. Listed systems may be placed in residential and commercial districts at the 20 and 50 kWh per-unit caps, which forces the player to build many small distributed units instead of one big one, and that distributed topology is itself more resilient to a single fire. Explosion control from the third edition converts a catastrophic enclosure rupture into a contained vent event.

standards.title: Standard for Test Method for Evaluating Thermal Runaway Fire Propagation in Battery Energy Storage Systems
standards.bodyFull: UL Standards & Engagement (binational ANSI and Standards Council of Canada standard)
standards.edition: Published 2025-03-12 (fifth edition), superseding the 2019 fourth edition
standards.what: A TEST METHOD, not a certification: there is no UL 9540A listing and any product claiming one is misdescribing itself. It is the only consensus standard NFPA 855 names for large-scale fire testing, and its data is what an Authority Having Jurisdiction uses to set separation distances, enclosure configuration and fire protection when an installation exceeds the prescriptive code limits. It runs in four escalating levels: cell (force one cell into thermal runaway in a pressure vessel and analyse the vent gas by gas chromatography), module (does runaway propagate to neighbouring cells, and at what heat and gas release rate), unit, and installation (does the installed fire protection actually work, and what is the deflagration and re-ignition risk).
standards.why: The question of how far apart two battery containers must sit, and whether a fire in one takes the whole site, is decided by this test and nothing else.
standards.gameEffect: The mechanic that turns a battery site from a single sprite into a layout puzzle. Running the UL 9540A test costs money and time and returns a propagation number, and that number sets the minimum spacing grid for the site: a battery that fails module-level propagation must be placed with wide firebreaks, halving the energy the player can fit on a parcel; one that passes packs tight. Untested systems fall back to the code default spacing, which is deliberately punitive. When a thermal-runaway event fires, a tested-and-passed site loses one module; an untested site loses the whole installation and damages adjacent tiles.

standards.title: Safety of Nuclear Power Plants: Design
standards.bodyFull: International Atomic Energy Agency
standards.edition: Revision 1, 2016. Supersedes SSR-2/1 (2012), which superseded NS-R-1
standards.what: The design requirements for a nuclear power plant, derived from the IAEA Fundamental Safety Objective. It is where defence in depth is set out as an enforceable design requirement rather than a slogan: successive independent physical barriers and levels of protection, so that no single failure and no single human error defeats the plant. It covers the fundamental safety functions, the design basis, design extension conditions and the requirements on each plant system. Revision 1 came out of a review begun in 2011 after Fukushima Daiichi; the review found no significant area of weakness and produced a small set of amendments strengthening the requirements, which is itself the interesting result.
standards.why: Nuclear is the largest dispatchable low-carbon block a city can add, and whether it is an asset or a liability is decided almost entirely by whether the design safety requirements were met and enforced.
standards.gameEffect: Nuclear is unlockable only with SSR-2/1 adopted, and adoption sets the accident model. A plant built to the full defence-in-depth requirement survives the design-basis events (loss of offsite power, flood, seismic) with a scram and no release; a plant built to a cheaper national derogation has a small per-event chance of a release that renders surrounding tiles uninhabitable for the rest of the run. Design extension conditions specifically buy survival of the beyond-design-basis combined event (flood plus station blackout) that is the Fukushima case, and that upgrade costs about 15 percent of plant capital.

standards.title: Hydropower Sustainability Standard
standards.bodyFull: Hydropower Sustainability Council, administered by the Hydropower Sustainability Alliance with the International Hydropower Association
standards.edition: Launched 2021-09-08 at the World Hydropower Congress; current text version 1.2, October 2023
standards.what: A standard PLUS a certification scheme, and the distinction is worth keeping: it assesses a hydropower project against 12 environmental, social and governance topics at two performance levels, good practice (the minimum requirements) and best practice (the advanced requirements). Projects passing independent assessment may be labelled certified sustainable, and a project meeting all minimum requirements plus enough advanced ones can be recommended for Gold. It harmonises with the earlier Hydropower Sustainability Assessment Protocol and the Gap Analysis Tool. Certification is used to demonstrate alignment with Climate Bonds Initiative green bond requirements, the EU Taxonomy and World Bank and IFC performance standards.
standards.why: Hydropower is the largest source of renewable electricity in the world and also the one with the worst record on displacement, river ecology and downstream water rights. Whether a dam is a climate solution depends on questions this standard actually asks.
standards.gameEffect: Hydro projects can be built raw or certified. Raw hydro is cheaper and faster and generates a displacement and downstream-water penalty that suppresses population growth and raises unrest in affected districts for the rest of the run. Certified hydro costs about 20 percent more and takes longer to permit, but unlocks green bond financing at a lower interest rate and removes the unrest penalty. Gold certification additionally unlocks EU Taxonomy alignment, which the disclosure track needs.

standards.title: IEEE Standard for Interconnection and Interoperability of Distributed Energy Resources with Associated Electric Power Systems Interfaces
standards.bodyFull: Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Standards Association
standards.edition: 2018 edition with Amendment IEEE 1547a-2020; status confirmed Active on the IEEE SA record 2026-08-09
standards.what: The rules a distributed energy resource must obey to be allowed on the distribution grid, up to 10 MVA at the point of common coupling, technology-agnostic across inverters, batteries, fuel cells and rotating machines. The 2018 revision inverted the previous rule. Under IEEE 1547-2003 a DER had to disconnect within 2 seconds for any voltage between 0.5 and 0.88 per unit and was not allowed to regulate voltage at all, so a distant fault took every inverter on the feeder off at once.
